short_title: Ion mobility method for lipoprotein particles (method paper)

citation.title: Direct determination of lipoprotein particle sizes and concentrations by ion mobility analysis

access.abstract_only_note: Publisher full text returned 403. Total LDL particle number precision and the comparison of ion-mobility LDL-P with ApoB are not in the abstract.

study.design_detail: Description and analytical validation of gas-phase differential electrophoretic macromolecular mobility (ion mobility) after ultracentrifugation to remove albumin; results correlated with standard cholesterol and apolipoprotein methods.
study.population: Serum samples (number not stated in the abstract)

claims.statement: Upper bound of intra- and interassay CV for LDL particle size.

source_location.quote: Intra- and interassay coefficients of variation for LDL particle size were <1.0%.

claims.statement: Upper bound of intra- and interassay variation for LDL and HDL subfraction measurements.

source_location.quote: The intra- and interassay variation for LDL and HDL particle subfraction measurements was <20%.

claims.statement: Correlation of ion-mobility non-HDL particle measure with ApoB.

source_location.quote: IM-measured non-HDL correlated well with apolipoprotein B (r = 0.92).

findings_summary: Describes Quest Diagnostics' ion mobility method, which counts lipoprotein particles by size after ultracentrifugation. LDL particle size was highly precise (CV <1.0%); LDL and HDL subfraction measurements varied by up to <20% within and between assays; the ion-mobility non-HDL measure correlated with ApoB (r = 0.92).

limitations.text: Developed and validated by the laboratory that offers the test (author affiliation: Quest Diagnostics Nichols Institute).
The abstract reports precision for size and subfractions, not for total LDL particle number, and correlates ApoB with ion-mobility non-HDL rather than with LDL particle number.
A published comment and author reply exist (Clin Chem 2008;54:2086-2089); not reviewed.
The method has been refined since 2008 (Williams et al. 2014 report using 'refinements made subsequent to the methods original description').

applicability_constraints: Analytical characteristics of the 2008 method; current laboratory performance may differ.
A correlation coefficient describes agreement across samples, not the size of disagreement for one sample.
interpretation: Ion mobility counts particles by size, a different measurement principle from an ApoB protein assay; its subfraction measurements carry up to ~20% analytical variation, so a single subfraction value has wide uncertainty. The abstract does not say how ion-mobility LDL particle number compares in absolute terms with ApoB.

review.verified_by: Automated agent (Claude), interactive session; not an independent or clinical review
